I'll check what each of these constant writes does to the output vocabulary, using its single mean-write vector (mean activation × down column) projected through the tied unembedding, summarised as token-class counts among the 200 most promoted and most suppressed tokens. A unit whose constant write strongly suppresses digits, "####" or end-of-turn, or promotes some odd class, would be a mechanistic candidate. Mixed-vocabulary effects mean these are ordinary.

Nothing token-specific here. The large constant writers promote and suppress mixtures of English words versus non-ASCII tokens, and none target digits, "####" or end-of-turn, so they look like ordinary language/register bias units. Closing the bias-neuron line. The remaining structural place I haven't examined per component is attention heads. I'll compute, for each of the 104 query heads, the norms of its o_proj block and its q_proj block, compared within the layer and across layers. A head whose output was silenced or boosted would stand out as an outlier against its layer siblings, for example one head with near-zero o_proj norm or one 3× larger than the others. Uniform per-layer values would close weight-level head forensics, and I would then move to causal head-ablation screening with teacher-forced passes.

Per-head o_proj and q_proj norms are unremarkable: every head is within 0.68 to 1.44 of its layer mean. That closes weight-level forensics completely. Arithmetic is fine and there is no prompt-time switch, so a remaining possibility is a "mode" that turns on during generation in some answers and degrades the reasoning. Such a mode would appear in the answer-averaged residual stream as a principal component that is bimodal across answers, two clusters, and strongly tied to failure. Ordinary difficulty would instead give unimodal components with weak, graded correlation. For layers 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 I'll compute the top 10 PCs of the answer-mean residuals over the 445 finished answers. For each I'll report its correct-vs-wrong AUC and a bimodality coefficient (values above ~0.555 suggest two modes). A bimodal PC with AUC far from 0.5 (say <0.3 or >0.7) would localise a candidate mode direction for a causal test.

The first principal component at every layer (18 to 27% of the variance) is clearly bimodal: bimodality coefficient 0.60 to 0.79, against 0.3 to 0.45 for the other PCs. It also separates correct from wrong answers more than any other PC (AUC 0.31 to 0.36, i.e. 0.64 to 0.69 in the other direction). So answers fall into two regimes with different accuracy. The regimes might be harmless output styles (LaTeX/\boxed versus plain text, markdown headers), or a degraded "mode". I'll split the 445 finished answers into the two clusters by the sign of a 2-means split on PC0 at layer 12. For each cluster I'll report accuracy, size, mean length, and the frequency of style features: "####" marker, "\boxed", "$" LaTeX, "**" bold, "Step" headings. If the clusters differ mainly in a style feature and still differ in accuracy, the style regime itself is a candidate failure mechanism, which I can then test causally by steering between regimes. If accuracy is equal within style-matched answers, it is a confound.
